verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              ततो वाग्युद्धमभवत्तुमुलं जनमेजय। यत्र दुःखान्वितो राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said “At the outset, O Janamejaya, a dreadful encounter of words took place between the two heroes. With respect to that, king Dhritarashtra, filled with grief, said thisधिगस्तु खलु मानुष्यं यस्य निष्ठेयमीदृशी।

verses.sanskrit: धिगस्तु खलु मानुष्यं यस्य निष्ठेयमीदृशी। एकादश चमूभर्ता यज्ञ पुत्रो ममानघ॥२॥
आज्ञाप्य सर्वान्नृपतीन् भुक्त्वा चेमां वसुन्धराम्। गदामादाय वेगेन पदातिः प्रस्थितो रणे॥३॥
verses.english: He had all the kings under his command and had enjoyed the sovereignty of the whole Earth! Alas, he that had been so, was now reduced to a warrior proceeding to battle, on foot, shouldering his mace.

verses.sanskrit: भूत्वा हि जगतो नाथो ह्यनाथ इव मे सुतः। गदामुद्यम्य यो याति किमन्यद्भागधेयतः॥४॥
verses.english: My poor son, who had before been the lord of the universe, was now himself without help! Alas, he had, then, to proceed on foot, shouldering his mace! What can it be but Destiny? Alas, O Sanjaya, great was the grief that was felt by my son now! 'Having uttered these words, the king afflicted with great sorrow became silent.

verses.sanskrit: अहो दुःखं महत्प्राप्तं पुत्रेण मम सञ्जय। एवमुक्त्वा स दुःखार्तो विरराम जनाधिपः॥५॥

सञ्जय उवाच।
              स मेघनिनदो हर्षान्निनदन्निव गोवृषः। आजुहाव तदा पार्थं युद्धाय युधि वीर्यवान्॥६॥
भीममाह्वायमाने तु कुरुराजे महात्मानि। प्रादुरासन्सुघोराणि रूपाणि विविधान्युत॥७॥
verses.english: When the great king of the Kurus thus summoned Bhima to the encounter, various awful portents appeared there.

verses.sanskrit: ववुर्वाताः सनिर्घाताः पांशुवर्षं पपात च। बभूवुश्च दिशः सर्वास्तिमिरेण समावृताः॥८॥
verses.english: Fierce winds began to blow with loud noises at intervals, and a shower of dust fell. All the points of the compass were covered with a thick darkness.

verses.sanskrit: महास्वनाः सुनिर्वातास्तुमुला लोमहर्षणा। पेतुस्तथोल्काः शतशः स्फोटयन्त्यो नभस्तलात्॥९॥
verses.english: Thunder-bolts of loud noise dropped on all sides, causing a great confusion and making the very hair to stand on end. Hundreds of meteors fell, with a loud noise from the sky.

verses.sanskrit: राहुश्चाग्रसदादित्यमपर्वणि विशाम्पते। चकम्पे च महाकम्पं पृथिवी सवनद्रुमा॥१०॥
दीप्ताश्च वातः प्रववुर्नीचैः शर्करकर्षिणः। गिरीणां शिखराण्येव न्यपतन्त महीतले॥११॥
verses.english: Hot winds blew, carrying showers of hard pebbles along the ground. The summits of mountains dropped down on the Earth's surfacc.

verses.sanskrit: मृगा बहुविधाकाराः सम्पतन्ति दिशो दश। दीप्ताः शिवाश्चाप्यनदन् घोररूपाः सुदारुणाः॥१२॥
verses.english: Various Animals were seen to run in various directions. Terrible and fierce jackals, with firing mouths, yelled piteously.

verses.sanskrit: निर्घाताश्च महाघोरा बभूवुर्लोमहर्षणाः। दीप्तायां दिशि राजेन्द्र मृगाश्चाशुभवेदिनः॥१३॥
verses.english: Loud and terrific hair-stirring sounds were heard on every side, the four quarters seemed to be on fire, and many animals of ill omen became visible.

verses.sanskrit: उदपानगताश्चापो व्यवर्धन्त समन्ततः। अशरीरा महानादाः श्रूयन्ते स्म तदा नृप॥१४॥
verses.english: The water in the wells on all sides swelled up. Loud sounds came from every side without, O king, none to utter them being visible.

verses.sanskrit: एवमादीनि दृष्ट्वाऽऽथ निमित्तानि वृकोदरः। उवाच भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं धर्मराजं युधिष्ठिरम्॥१५॥
नैष शक्तो रणे जेतुं मन्दात्मा मां सुयोधनः। अद्य क्रोधं विमोक्ष्यामि विगूढं हृदये चिरम्॥१६॥
सुयोधने कौरवेन्द्रे खाण्डवे पावको तथा। शल्यमद्योद्धरिष्यामि तव पाण्डव हृच्छयम्॥१७॥
verses.english: I shall today pluck out the dart, O son of Pandu, that lay so long sticking to your heart. Be happy, O king, after I shall have struck down this wretch with my mace.

verses.sanskrit: निहत्य गदया पापमिमं कुरुकुलाधमम्। अद्य कीर्तिमयीं मालां प्रतिमोक्ष्याम्यहं त्वयि॥१८॥
verses.english: Killing with my mace this sinful wretch of Kuru's race, I shall to-day, place around your neck the garland of Fame!

verses.sanskrit: हत्वेमं पापकर्माणं गदया रणमूर्धनि। अद्यास्य शतधा देहं भिनद्मि गदयाऽनया॥१९॥
verses.english: Killing this sinful person with my mace on the field of battle, I shall to-day, with this very mace of mine, break his body into a hundred pieces! He shall not have again to enter the city of Hastinapur!

verses.sanskrit: नायं प्रवेष्टा नगरं पुनर्वारणसाह्वयम्। सर्पोत्सर्गस्य शयने विषदानस्य भोजने।॥२०॥
प्रमाणकोट्यां पातस्य दाहस्य जतुवेश्मनि। सभायामवहासस्य सर्वस्वहरणस्य च॥२१॥
verses.english: The setting of serpents at us while we were sleeping, the giving of venom to us while we were eating, the casting of our body into the water at Pramanakoti, the attempt to burn us at the house of lac, the insult given to us at the assembly, the robbing us of all our wealth, the whole year of our living in concealment, our exile into the forest, O sinless one, of all these misfortunes, O best of Bharata's race, I shall terminate to-day, O Bharata's chief! Killing this wretch, I shall, in one single day, pay off all the debts I owe him.

verses.sanskrit: वर्षमज्ञातवासस्य वनवासस्य चानघ। अद्यान्तमेषां दुःखानां गन्ताहं भरतर्षभ॥२२॥
एकाह्रा विनिहत्येमं भविष्याम्यात्मनोऽनृणः। अद्यायुर्धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्मतेरकृतात्मनः॥२३॥
समाप्तं भरतश्रेष्ठ मातापित्रोश्च दर्शनम्। अद्य सौख्यं तु राजेन्द्र कुरुराजस्य दुर्मतेः॥२४॥
verses.english: To-day the lease of life, of this wicked son of Dhritarashtra, of impure soul, has reached its end, O Bharata's chief. After this day he shall not again look at his father and mother!

verses.sanskrit: समाप्तं च महाराज नारीणां दर्शनं पुनः। अद्यायं कुरुराजस्य शान्तनोः कुलपांसनः॥२५॥
verses.english: To-day, O king, the happiness of this wicked king of the Kurus has terminated. After this day, O king, he shall not again see a beautiful damsel!

verses.sanskrit: प्राणान् श्रियं च राज्यं च त्यक्त्वा शेष्यति भूतले। राजा च धृतराष्ट्रोऽद्य श्रुत्वा पुत्रं निपातितम्॥२६॥
verses.english: To-day this disgrace of Shantanu's race shall sleep on the naked Earth, his life, his prosperity, and his kingdom gone!

verses.sanskrit: स्मरिष्यत्यशुभं कर्म यत्तच्छकुनिबुद्धिजम्। इत्युक्त्वा राजशार्दूल गदामादाय वीर्यवान्॥२७॥
verses.english: Today hearing of his son's death, king Dhritarashtra will remember all those wrongs that he did to us under Shakuni's advice."

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यतिष्ठत युद्धाय शक्रो वृत्रमिवाह्वयन्। तमुद्यतगदं दृष्ट्वा कैलासमिव शृङ्गिणम्॥२८॥
verses.english: Having said these words, that energetic prince, of Bharata's race, stood up for battle, like Shakra summoning Vritra to an encounter.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनः पुनः क्रुद्धो दुर्योधनमुवाच ह। राज्ञश्च धृतराष्ट्रस्य तथा त्वमपि चात्मनः॥२९॥
verses.english: Seeing Duryodhana also standing with uplifted mace like mount Kailasa, Bhimasena, worked up with ire, once more addressed him, saying— 'Remember that misdeed of yourself and king Dhritarashtra that occurred at Varnavata!

verses.sanskrit: स्पर तद्दुष्कृतं कर्म यद्वृत्तं वारणावते। द्रौपदी च परिक्लिष्टा सभामध्ये रजस्वला॥३०॥
द्यूते न वञ्चितो राजा यत्त्वया सौबलेन च। वने दुःखं च यत्प्राप्तमस्माभिस्त्वत्कृतं महत्॥३१॥
verses.english: Remember the ill-treatment of Draupadi, while in her season, in the midst of the assembly! Remember how yourself and Subala's son deprived the king at dice.

verses.sanskrit: विराटनगरे चैव योन्यन्तरगतैरिव। तत्सर्वं पातयाम्यद्य दिष्ट्या दृष्टोऽसि दुर्मते॥३२॥
verses.english: Remember the great misfortune suffered by L'S, for you, in the forest, as also in Virata's city, as if we had once more entered the womb! I shall avenge them all to-day. By good luck, I see you to-day!

verses.sanskrit: त्वत्कृतेऽसौ हतः शेते शरतल्पे प्रतापवान्। गाङ्गेयो रथिनां श्रेष्ठो निहतो याज्ञसेनिना॥३३॥
हतो द्रोणश्च कर्णश्च तथा शल्यः प्रतापवान्। वैराग्नेरादिकर्तासौ शकुनिः सौबलो हतः॥३४॥
verses.english: Drona also has been killed, and Karna, and Shalya of great prowess! Subala's son Shakuni too, that root of all this evil has been killed!

verses.sanskrit: प्रातिकामी तथा पापो द्रौपद्याः क्लेशकृद्धतः। भ्रातरस्ते हताः सर्वे शूरा विक्रान्तयोधिनः॥३५॥
एते चान्ये च बहवो निहतास्त्वत्कृते नृपाः। त्वामद्य निहनिष्यामि गदया नात्र संशयः॥३६॥
verses.english: These and many other kings have been killed through your fault! I shall kill you to-day with my mace! There is not the least doubt about it!'

verses.sanskrit: इत्येवमुच्चै राजेन्द्र भाषमाणं वृकोदरम्। उवाच गतभी राजन् पुत्रस्ते सत्यविक्रमः॥३७॥
verses.english: While Vrikodara, O king, was uttering these words in a loud voice, your fearless son answered him, saying-'What is the use of bragging? Fight me, O Vrikodara! O wretch, to-day I shall satiate your desire of fight!

verses.sanskrit: किं कत्थनेन बहुना युध्यस्व त्वं वृकोदर। अद्य तेऽहं विनेष्यामि युद्धश्रद्धां कुलाधम॥३८॥
न हि दुर्योधनः क्षुद्र केनचित्त्वद्विधेन वै। शक्यस्त्रासयितुं वाचां यथाऽन्यः प्राकृतो नरः॥३९॥
verses.english: Mean as you are, know that Duryodhana is not capable, like an ordinary person, of being terrified by a person like you!

verses.sanskrit: चिरकालेप्सितं दिष्ट्या हृदयस्थमिदं मम। त्वया सह गदायुद्धं त्रिदशैरुपपादितम्॥४०॥
verses.english: For a long time have I cherished this desire! For a long time I have been cherishing this desire! By good fortune the goods have at last brought it about!

verses.sanskrit: किं वाचा बहुनोक्तेन कत्थितेन च दुर्मते। वाणी सम्पद्यतामेषा कर्मणा मा चिरं कृथाः॥४१॥
verses.english: What is the use of long talks and idle brag, O wicked man! Carry out these words of yours into acts! Do not delay at all!—Hearing these words of his, the Somakas and the other kings that were present there, all praised them highly.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्व एवाभ्यपूजयन्। राजानः सोमकाश्चैव ये तत्रासन् समागताः॥४२॥
ततः सम्पूजितः सर्वैः सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः। भूयो धीरां मतिं चक्रे युद्धाय कुरुनन्दनः॥४३॥
verses.english: Lauded by all, Duryodha's hair stood erect with joy, and he made of his mind for fight.

verses.sanskrit: उन्मत्तमिव मातङ्गं तलशब्दैर्नराधिपाः। भूयः संहर्षयाञ्चक्रुर्दुर्योधनममर्षणम्॥४४॥
verses.english: The kings present once again cheered your wrathful son with claps like persons exciting a mad elephant to a fight.

verses.sanskrit: तं महात्मा महात्मानं गदामुद्यम्य पाण्डवः। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन धार्तराष्ट्रं वृकोदरः॥४५॥
बृंहन्ति कुञ्जरास्तत्र हया ह्रेषन्ति चासकृत्। शस्त्राणि चाप्यदीप्यन्त पाण्डवानां जयैषिणाम्॥४६॥
